proof_summary: For $p\equiv3\pmod4$, reindexing by quadratic residues turns the matrix into columns drawn from the commuting Paley matrices $\chi(r-s)$ and $\chi(r+s)$; a product-parity count makes the skew-symmetric principal part odd-dimensional, forcing the determinant to vanish. For $p\equiv1\pmod4$, Euler’s criterion reduces the entries modulo $p$ to $(x_i-Cy_j)^m$, whose binomial expansion factors the matrix into a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix and a nonsingular moment matrix, with Wilson’s theorem ($C^2=-1$) ensuring the remaining scalar obstruction is nonzero.
